sections.text: I enter this world and animate all My creatures with My vitality; and by My cool moonbeams I nourish the plants.
Becoming the fire of life, I pass into their bodies and, uniting with the vital streams of Prana and Apana, I digest the various kinds of food.
I am enthroned in the hearts of all; memory, wisdom and discrimination owe their origins to Me. I am He Who is to be realised in the scriptures; I inspire their wisdom and I know their truth.

So we had been discussing chapter 15, Purushottama Yoga, Yoga of the Supreme Being. And so far we have seen Bhagavan saying that everything that you see, everything that you can perceive, and everything that you can experience is nothing but me. In the last few verses we have seen he said: the light which is from the sun, which illumines this entire world of yours, is nothing but my light -- it comes from me alone.
The light from the moon which nourishes the plants is nothing but my own light. And the fertility in this soil which supports all the beings on this planet is nothing but me. My mind, my intellect, which is aware of this world -- That awareness comes from him.
And this world which I experience also comes from him. Then he says, not only that this being is supported by me, but all this functions within the sentient beings which makes them living beings. I support those functions.
Aham Vaishva Narobhatva Prani Namdha Masridha. Residing in the bodies of all the beings, I digest these four types of food. Basically, as I said, our ancestors were fond of classification, so they always have some classification.
Foods are of four types. And once you look at what the four types of foods are, theres nothing left out. So any food that a being can eat, it gets digested.
Bhagavan said, by me residing in this body as this eternal fire, this internal fire. So everything I see, everything I hear, everything I experience -- there is really nothing other than the Lord. And this somewhat, if you really think logically fits into the normal belief, a normal declaration in all religion that the God is omnipresent.
Once something we have taken as omnipresent, there is no room left for anything else. So if we say that God is omnipresent in this world, then there is no room for you and I as an individual other than God. As we have discussed so many times from the physics perspective, if I say I am omnipresent in my chair, there is no room for anything else or anybody else.
So now everything in this chair has to be me. Whether its my leg, its my hand, my torso, whatever, its all me. So Bhagavan said, I am omnipresent.
And therefore all the experiences illumined by your consciousness is nothing but me alone. So we have so far seen Bhagavan is giving his identity. What is the identity of the supreme Being? That there is none other than that being exist.
So the last verse 14 we say prani nam deha masirithah prana pana samayukta Pachami annam Chaturvedam. I can see at the macro level that the Lord is everywhere. At the micro level, the Lord is also in my body.
This body, mind and intellect come from this world. This world is nothing but his expression. But the functions within me -- which I think differentiate me from the insentient world called matter -- make me consider myself as something completely different than matter.
Thats why my body is so spatial. Because I dont think its a matter. I consider thats me.
But that me from the matter to me is because of these functions which makes me a living being. These pranas and apanas, all these activities happening in my body. And Bhagawan says that also I control by living in your body.
In the next verse it says, Sarvasya chaham Hrudhisan niveshtah matthaha smriti gnanam upo hanamcha vedeshcha sarve ham eva vedyo vedantakrut veda Videva chaham. So what is my relationship to the Lord now? He said, I am residing in the hearts of all beings. How do I know? This great Lord is everywhere, and that may overwhelm my intellect.
I am a seeker seeking my experience or realization of my Lord. Now he says, the light of the sun is me, the light of the moon is me. I am the fertility in the earth.
Then we give up and say, I will never be able to reach him. Somebody says, Rajan, if you want to do something, why dont you call up the President? If you tell me to call a project manager, I can think about it. But make a cold call to the President of the United States, Barack Obama? That really doesnt sound like a practical thing to do.
So we say, well, if Bhagavan is so supreme, then there is no way that Ill ever be able to get connected with him. So now Bhagawan said, no, thats not the truth. The truth is Im residing in the hearts of all beings.
Sarvasenni, Vistaha, Matthaha, Smrutihi, Gnanam and Upohanam. Because Im residing in the hearts of all beings. And because of me they have a memory.
Because of me they have knowledge. And because of me they have forgetfulness or ignorance. Everything which I know today is because of my consciousness.
Im aware of my experiences, so it becomes my memory. Im aware of what I have learned. So my memory has become my knowledge.
If somebody says what month comes after January? Well, I learned in kg, its February. Thats nothing but my memory. I consider that as my knowledge.
But its actually my memory. All this, Bhagavan said, comes from me. I will only remember if Im conscious.
Without that, I wont. But more important than this knowledge is also forgetfulness. If I remember everything that happened, there wont be any room for me to learn anything new.
The IT guys were telling me, Rajan, our server is really getting to capacity now. We had been in business for 12 years and we keep piling all this data on it. I think its a time for you to change the server. Its 80% capacity you really have to have.
So I said, well, Ill tell you what. We cant really afford a new server right now. Purge all the old projects which are done five years ago.
I dont need them anymore. Purge them so I can put new projects onto my server. Forgetfulness is the gift from God to us.
If we dont forget, we will not be able to learn anything new. All the bad memories of our childhood literally get erased from us. Thats why we also recall our childhood as so good.
My college days were so good. Because the bad memories are erased. What you remember is all the fun you had.
Now there are some bad memories that remain there. But most of it get erased. So I had a nice childhood when I was growing up.
Because the Bhagavan has given a gift of forgetting things which is not useful to you. Forgetting things which removes all the unnecessary ignorance out of your mind. So you can fill that void with new knowledge.
Sarvasya Chaham Rudhisa Nivestaha. I am residing in the hearts of all. So we obviously in my heart Bhagavan is here.
And obviously you and I can logically say heart is not that physiological organ literally pumping the blood. It is the core of my being. What I consider me is my heart.
What is at the heart of Richmond city? What is at the heart of this community? What I consider the core of my being. Bhagavan said, I reside there. The core of my being is my awareness about me.
My awareness about me, makes me who I am. That has these good qualities about compassion, charity, love. But once I decide in there, when my God is invoked then I will have this good quality manifest.
When I am in a divine mood, then I will have love, compassion, charity, all the good qualities. When I am forgetting about my Lord, my being, then I will have all the negative qualities. Because those negative qualities are the product of my ignorance.
I hate somebody, Im evil to someone. All these things are because of the lack of my connection with my core of my being, my heart, my Lord who makes me who I am. So Bhagavan says, Sarvasyacham, Hrudhi Sanniveshtah.
I am residing in all the beings at the core of their heart. When I am really aware of myself, I can only manifest my divine qualities -- love, compassion, charity. Whatever the good qualities we think of.
Its only when Im devoid of those connections that I will have jealousy, hatred. He said, Matthaha Smritih. Because of me is the memory.
Because of me is the knowledge. Because Im aware of myself, I have a memory. Because Im aware of myself, I have a knowledge.
And because Im aware of myself, I have forgetfulness. I am also our ignorance. I am as much aware of my knowledge as I am aware of my ignorance. Rajan, do you know medicine? No, I know nothing about it. Do you know architecture? Yes, tell me all about it. I am aware of my knowledge.
I am also aware of my ignorance. Bhagavan said, its all because of my presence in you, the consciousness. I reside in you as your being.
I am the Vedas and I am that needs to be known. I am the author of the Vedanta and knower of the Vedas. Now Vedas, as we have seen, they are our scriptures.
What do they represent? They represent knowledge. The knowledge compiled by the sages becomes Veda. This knowledge encompass everything.
Utilitarian knowledge as well as the divine knowledge, secular as well as sacred. Now the secular knowledge obviously also come from my awareness. I learn things and I use it.
I am all this knowledge that is out there. And I am only the one to be known. And Veda in the end says what? The only thing to be known is your own self.
Once you realize yourself, there is nothing more to be known. Having reached that place, we have learned that no one comes back. Thats what Veda says.
Thats what Vedanta said. In the end of Veda, the section which deals with the Upanishads and the knowledge about yourself is called Vedanta. So who gave this knowledge of the self to the Rishis? Bhagavan said, I did.
And therefore there is no authorship in our Vedas of who wrote this Vedanta. There is no authorship because it is a revealed knowledge. That is what is remembered.
So I can say I thought about it many times. Honestly, I can tell you, I give some examples in my lectures. And I really sometimes feel good that I really thought about really neat example.
Then I read s commentary and I find the exact same example in it. I said, how did that happen? I thought, I thought about it. What I really forget is Id been listening to since I was 16 years old.
So all this thing which I think, Im thinking fresh, new is literally come from what I heard since I was 16 year old. Now, I may not have understood the time, I may not have got the gist of it at the time, but things stay with you. Then we are really churning on that idea.
Things come out and now you think, I invented this idea. And therefore in Hinduism there is no originality. The only originality is with him.
Everything else we do is just relearn. So Bhagavan says, therefore I am the author of Vedanta. Now I am the one to be known.
Everything which I can consider is the quest of my life. If Bhagavan said, is me, know that I am at the core of your being. So how difficult would it be for you to know your core of your being? Not that difficult, Bhagavan said, as long as you turn your gaze towards yourself.
So these verses are obviously very contemplative verses and not really intellectual verses, but contemplative verses. But going back to our understanding of what is real, what is unreal, what is transitory or temporary, and what is permanent.

These verses reveal the Supreme Person as the sustainer of all existence at every level - cosmic, earthly, and personal. Krishna declares that He enters the earth and sustains all beings with His energy, becomes the moon (Soma) and nourishes all plants with life-giving essence, and as the digestive fire (Vaishvanara) within all living beings, digests the four kinds of food. This teaching dissolves the boundary between sacred and mundane. The very act of digestion happening in your body right now is a divine function. The next time you eat, consider: the fire that transforms food into energy is not merely a biological process but the Lord functioning within you through prana and apana.
Verse 15 is especially intimate: Sarvasya chaham hridi sannivishto - I am seated in the hearts of all beings. From Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal. This means your capacity to remember, to know, and even to forget is a divine gift. Forgetfulness, often seen as a flaw, is actually a blessing - it allows old wounds to heal and makes room for new learning. The verse concludes by stating that the Lord is what is to be known through all the Vedas, is the author of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas. Today, reflect: if the Supreme dwells in my heart as the source of all my knowing, how far do I need to search? Turn your attention inward, to the very awareness that makes all experience possible, and recognize that the goal of all seeking is already present as the seeker.
